Subject: Post-demo: model fit follow-up & quantization tradeoffs

Hi Samir / Natalie 

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can get you a hands-on eval this week: 

1) Summary of fit
- Primary workload: clinical note summarization + question answering across 1k-5k token contexts.
- Key constraints: sub-200ms per-token p99 latency for read ops when on Dedicated, and strict quality thresholds for clinical extracts (factuality + hallucination minimization).

2) Suggested initial models to evaluate (we'll provide prompt sets + metrics):
- redwood-medium-v2 (fast baseline, FP16/FP8 friendly)
- llama2-13b-AWQ (good cost/quality tradeoff on AWQ)
- ggml-l13b-rev2 (FP8 paths; higher throughput for batch workloads)

3) Quantization/throughput topics to validate
- AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8: expected throughput, memory, and typical quality delta on your prompt set.
- We'll run a small trade study on your sample prompts to surface any regressions and suggested mitigations (prompt tuning / constrained decoding / fallback policies).

Next steps I propose:
- I attach a short benchmark summary and the prompt-set we'll use for Atlas Health evals (attached: 20260310-redwood-benchmark-summary.pdf, prompt-set-atlas-v1.jsonl).
- Can we schedule a 60-min hands-on eval with your ML lead (Priya?) on Fri 3/12? We'll run the trade study live and go over config recommendations.
- We'll also prepare a Dedicated capacity quote if we see the latency/throughput match your SLOs.

If this looks good, I'll loop in our solutions engineer (Dev) to prep the quantization configs and run the initial AWQ/GPTQ comparisons.

Thanks 
Marissa

Thanks Marissa  helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side before the hands-on:

Samir 

Great questions. High-level answers here and I'll have Dev send concrete numbers and config snippets before the session. Attached: quantization-tradeoffs-q1.pdf (short memo).

- Latency / throughput expectations:
  - On Dedicated with 13B-class models: AWQ typically reduces memory footprint enabling higher batch sizes; p99 per-token latency often remains within ~1.1-1.4x of FP16 when using our optimized kernels, but exact numbers depend on sequence lengths and batching. For short prompts (<=256 tokens) and 10 concurrent users, you should expect p99 in the ~120-260ms range depending on choice of model and whether KV cache hits apply.

- Quality regressions:
  - Our trade studies show AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 can introduce small token-level distribution shifts, visible on sensitive clinical QA prompts. Typical impact: a ~1-3% drop in exact-match QA metrics for affected prompts; hallucination risk rises primarily on edge cases with ambiguous context. We'll surface the failing examples from your prompt set and recommend mitigations (constrained decoding, higher temperature safeguards, or falling back to FP16 for critical queries).

- Recommended approach for Atlas Health:
  1) Run an initial AWQ pass on your prompt-set (we'll do this in the hands-on). If regressions are acceptable, keep AWQ for production to reduce costs.
  2) For critical paths (clinical extractors), keep an FP16 or FP8-safe fallback route for queries that score low on confidence.
  3) Autoscale config: start with 1.5x baseline GPUs for daytime throughput and a higher-burst policy for nightly batch scoring. We'll share a draft autoscale policy after the session.

Links and artifacts:
- Shared benchmark folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-benchmarks
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/DL-2026-0132

I'll have Dev send the AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 numbers shortly. Looking forward to Fri  if Priya confirms, I'll put the invite on calendar.

Marissa

Subject: AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 quick numbers + config snippets

Hi all  looping in the recommended configs and quick numbers from our internal trade study (summary below). Attachment: awq-config-snippets.txt.

Summary (13B-class models on NVIDIA A10g / T4 family):
- FP16 baseline (redwood-medium-v2): ~18-25 tok/s per GPU (seq len 256), p99 per-token ~80-130ms depending on concurrencies.
- AWQ (llama2-13b-AWQ): ~28-40 tok/s per GPU (seq len 256), p99 ~110-200ms. Quality delta: small (1-2% EM drop on our clinical QM set).
- FP8 binary path (ggml-l13b-rev2-like): ~35-50 tok/s per device in optimized runtime; p99 ~100-180ms for batch scoring; quality delta wider on edge-case prompts (~2-4% EM drop).
- GPTQ results vary more by implementation; expect throughput between AWQ and FP8 with similar quality deltas.

Recommended quick configs:
- For low-latency user-facing: redwood-medium-v2 FP16 on Dedicated with small batch sizes (batch=1-2), KV cache enabled, autoscale min=2, max=6.
- For cost-optimized nightly batches: ggml-l13b-rev2 FP8 with batch=16-32, sequential pipelining.
- Fallback routing: tag critical routes to use FP16 model variant when confidence<0.6.

I'll bring a small notebook to the Fri session to run these on your sample prompts and show the exact diffs in outputs so Priya can inspect failing cases quickly.
